title: Caythorpe Heath Stirling Memorial
crew_summary: 4 killed (1 survived); pilot Flt Sgt. Joseph John Gordon Nicholson

external_narratives.summary: Memorial record for the crew of Stirling LJ450 at Caythorpe Heath. The aircraft from 1654 HCU was shot down by a Luftwaffe Me410 intruder during a night navigation and bombing exercise on 12 April 1944.
key_details: Shot down by Me410 intruder piloted by Hptm Dietrich Puttfarken (II/KG51)
Night navigation exercise with bombing practice on Bassingham Fen range
external_narratives.link_description: The poignant memorial record for Stirling LJ450 crew at Caythorpe Heath.

external_narratives.summary: Official heritage record for the Short Stirling aircraft crash site and memorial at Caythorpe. Crash site covered by a small copse maintained as a memorial to the crew.
key_details: Crash site copse preserved as memorial

The memorial was unveiled on July 7, 2004, by Mr.

This memorial was unveiled on 7 July 2004 by Mr David Theaker and GP Capt MP Colley, Station Commander RAF Cranwell.

Unveiling Ceremony (07 July 2004): The Short Stirling LJ450 memorial was unveiled during this ceremony.

Memorial Erection/Unveiling (7 Jul 2004): Erected and unveiled of the inscribed anodised aluminium plate with wooden frame on a wooden post on the edge of a spinney on the farm.
narrative: This memorial honors the crew of "Auben Fox," a Stirling Mk Heavy Bomber, registration LJ450, from 1654 HCU. On April 1, 1944, at 0125 hours, during a routine training flight, it was shot down by a Messerschmitt BF109 from 11/KG51's "Immelmann Squadron." Despite the loss of their aircraft, all crew members safely bailed out and sustained no injuries. David Theaker and Group Captain MP Colley, Station Commander RAF Cranwell. It stands as a tribute, left undisturbed at the crash site, in respect for their sacrifice, witnessed by the Theaker family.
